assumptions: The XML is RDML v1.0 to v1.4, uncompressed.
limits: Reads what the instrument wrote; it does not judge it.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: A file reader: the runs and the table come back as the RDML file states them, and the analyses that read them (call_cq, relative_expression, analyze_melt_curves) carry the reading.
bio.jane/contract.question: What does an RDML export hold, and what are one run's curves, Cq values, melts and partition counts as tables?

description: Read an instrument's RDML export - the open qPCR exchange standard, v1.0 to v1.4 - and hand back one run's contents as the same tables every other qPCR tool here takes. This is the step every qPCR analysis starts from. Lists what each run actually holds (amplification curves, melting curves, instrument Cq values, digital-PCR partition counts with the partition volume the file declares) before anything is imported, so a run is chosen on what is in it rather than on its name. Takes the UNCOMPRESSED XML: a `.rdml` archive is a zip, and the tool vocabulary here has no file input.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

rdml_xml.description: the RDML document as XML text - the `rdml_data.xml` member of a `.rdml` archive, or a bare `.xml` export. Not base64 and not a file path.

run.description: which run to read, 0-based across every experiment in the file in document order. A file routinely holds several; `summary` lists them all whatever this is set to.

table.description: which table to return for the chosen run. `summary` reads the file without importing anything. The other four are exactly what the panel's four `Send to ...` buttons produce, so a value imported here and one imported there cannot differ. Values: summary (Summary - what every run in the file holds), curves (Amplification curves - Cycle,<reaction>,...), cq (Instrument Cq values - the wide Ct table plus its group column), genorm (Instrument Cq values - long Target,Sample,Cq), melt (Melting curves - Temperature,<reaction>,...), partitions (Digital PCR partition counts - Well,Sample,Target,Positives,Partitions).

name: read_rdml_run

groups.description: for `cq`: one sample name per row of the Ct table, already aligned to it. The group column relative quantification needs

omitted.description: what the import deliberately left out and why - wells whose Cq is RDML's -1 `not available`, and samples whose replicates do not square up across targets. Never padded and never zero-filled (a Ct of 0 is a fabricated measurement)

rows.description: data rows in `table`, excluding its header

runs.description: every run in the file and what it holds - reactions, curves, melt curves, instrument Cq values, partition counts, the declared partition volumes, targets and samples

table.description: the chosen run's table, as the text the matching tool's own parser takes. Empty when the run has nothing of that kind - which is a fact about the run, not a failure

version.description: the RDML version the file declares (1.0-1.4). The reader's behaviour differs by version and a table without it is not reproducible
